attachments.origin_landmark: calcaneus (dorsal surface, medial-most slip of the EDB mass)
attachments.insertion_landmark: proximal phalanx of the great toe, base, dorsal surface

functional_compartments.name: Single fiber population
functional_compartments.function_note: Most medial slip of the same muscle mass as extensor digitorum brevis, sometimes described as its most differentiated part rather than a fully separate muscle.
functional_compartments.source: Ward SR, Eng CM, Smallwood LH, Lieber RL (2009) Clin Orthop Relat Res 467:1074-1082 -- lower-extremity muscle architecture (fascicle length, PCSA, sarcomere length) cadaver dataset

source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998); Ward SR, Eng CM, Smallwood LH, Lieber RL (2009) Clin Orthop Relat Res 467:1074-1082 -- lower-extremity muscle architecture (fascicle length, PCSA, sarcomere length) cadaver dataset

trigger_points.location_description: The medial belly of the extensor digitorum brevis/extensor hallucis brevis muscle mass, on the dorsum of the foot medial to the main EDB belly.
trigger_points.referred_pain_pattern: Locally confined pain over the dorsum of the foot near the base of the great toe, without the far-reaching referral typical of the leg muscles -- consistent with the local, non-distant referral Travell & Simons describe for this muscle mass as a whole.
trigger_points.activation_perpetuating_factors: Poor-fitting footwear, walking/running on uneven surfaces, and ankle/forefoot sprain.
trigger_points.notes: Travell & Simons and most secondary sources treat extensor hallucis brevis together with extensor digitorum brevis as a single muscle mass rather than describing a fully separate trigger point/referral pattern for it; can be mistaken for extensor tendinopathy or first MTP joint pathology.
trigger_points.source: Simons, Travell & Simons Trigger Point Manual, Vol. 2 (Lower Extremities), 1999 -- as cited in secondary summaries (e.g. Morningside Acupuncture NYC 'Extensor Hallucis Brevis Trigger Points', Niel Asher Education 'Trigger Point Therapy - Superficial Muscles of the Foot') describing extensor hallucis brevis as part of the same dorsal-foot muscle mass as extensor digitorum brevis with a locally confined referral pattern
